blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: While dataset distillation has witnessed significant advances in image classification, its extension to dense prediction tasks such as semantic segmentation is plagued by two core bottlenecks: bi-level optimization-based approaches suffer from prohibitive computational costs stemming from pixel-wise gradient unrolling, whereas proxy-based generative methods merely infuse visual textures into fixed semantic masks derived from real data, thus failing to condense rich semantic knowledge into a compact set of informative, novel scene generations. To address both bottlenecks simultaneously, we propose a novel Sample-Set Reinforcement Learning (S$^2$-RL) framework for generative semantic segmentation dataset distillation (SSDD). Specifically, S$^2$-RL formulates SSDD as a diffusion model based text-to-image generation paradigm, enabling flexible generation of images with informative, novel semantic distributions via a concise text prompt. Furthermore, we fine-tune a diffusion policy via Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), leveraging a sample-set dual reward paradigm: for individual samples, it enforces semantic alignment with input text prompts and intra-class feature diversity; for sample sets, it maximizes inter-sample semantic distribution diversity by solving a contextual multi-armed bandit problem. These design choices enable S$^2$-RL to distill large-scale semantic segmentation datasets into a compact set of generated samples that encapsulate diverse, informative semantic knowledge without the need of pixel-wise gradient unrolling. Extensive experiments on the ADE20K and COCO datasets demonstrate that S$^2$-RL achieves substantial and consistent improvements over state-of-the-art baselines, establishing a new benchmark for SSDD.
blocks.zh: 虽然数据集蒸馏法在图像分类方面取得了显著进展,但其延伸至语义分解等密集的预测任务却被两个核心瓶颈所困扰:双层优化方法因像素梯度不滚动而承受了令人望而生畏的计算成本;而代用基因方法仅仅将视觉纹理注入从真实数据中衍生出来的固定语义口罩中,从而未能将丰富的语义知识收缩成一套精密的,内容丰富的新颖的场景代. 为了同时解决这两个瓶颈问题,我们提出了一个关于基因语义分解数据集分馏(SSDD)的新的 " 样本-成套强化学习 " (S$^2$-RL)框架。 具体而言,S$^2$-RL将SSDD制定为一种基于文本到图像生成范式的传播模式,通过简洁的文本提示,能够灵活地生成具有信息化和新语义的图像。 此外,我们通过 " 集团相对政策优化 " (GRPO)对传播政策进行微调,利用样本组合的双重奖励模式:对于单个样本,它执行语义上与输入文本提示和类内特征多样性的一致;对于样本组合,它通过解决背景多武装强盗问题,最大限度地实现样本间语义分布多样性。 这些设计选择使S$^2$-RL能够将大规模语义分解数据集分解成一组紧凑而成的样本,这些样本囊括了多样的,信息化的语义知识而无需像素梯度解滚. 对ADE20K和COCO数据集的广泛实验表明,S$^2$-RL比最先进的基线取得了实质性和一致的改进,为SSDD建立了一个新的基准。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Data-efficient learning has become crucial as deep learning models grow increasingly data-hungry. Dataset distillation [ 40 ] addresses this by condensing massive datasets into compact synthetic surrogates. Existing advances in dataset distillation fall into two primary paradigms: optimization-based methods and proxy-based generative methods. While both paradigms yield strong performance on image classification, their extension to dense prediction tasks such as semantic segmentation remains fraught with substantial challenges.
blocks.zh: 随着深层学习模式越来越缺乏数据,提高数据效率的学习变得至关重要。 数据集分馏[40]通过将大规模数据集收缩为紧凑的合成代位来解决这个问题. 数据集蒸馏法的现有进步分为两大范式:以优化为基础的方法和以代用基因为基础的方法. 虽然这两个范式在图像分类方面都产生很强的性能,但其延伸至语义分解等密集的预测任务仍然充满了巨大的挑战.

blocks.en: Specifically, optimization-based methods (Figure 1(a) ), such as gradient matching [ 48 , 3 , 50 ] and distribution matching [ 39 , 49 , 28 ] , formulate dataset distillation as a bi-level optimization problem aiming to align the gradients or distributions of student models on synthetic data with those on the real counterpart. While theoretically rigorous, these methods suffer from computational intractability in semantic segmentation tasks. Unlike image classification, which only relies on sparse supervision, semantic segmentation requires unrolling pixel-wise gradients at full spatial resolution, leading to severe memory overhead and making end-to-end optimization practically infeasible.
blocks.zh: 具体而言,基于优化的方法(图1(a)),如梯度匹配[48,3,50]和分布匹配[39,49,28],制定数据集分馏作为双级优化问题,旨在将学生模型在合成数据上的梯度或分布与真实对应数据的梯度相匹配. 这些方法虽然在理论上很严格,但在语义分解任务中却存在计算不相容性. 与图像分类只依赖稀疏的监管不同,语义分解需要在全空间分辨率下不滚动像素-明智梯度,导致严重的内存超高,使端到端优化实际上不可行.

blocks.en: To circumvent this memory bottleneck, proxy-based generative methods [ 45 , 35 ] (Figure 1(b) ) have emerged as an efficient alternative, which bypass bi-level optimization via data inversion or global statistic matching. Since global statistics matching cannot comprehensively depict the complex spatial arrangements of multiple categories, existing approaches, such as those for object detection [ 27 ] or universal dataset distillation [ 26 ] , turn to rely on fixed spatial masks from real data for structural regularization. This strategy reduces the model to a mere texture filler within static boundaries, rather than a genuine scene composer, and thus fails to synthesize a compact set of novel, informative spatial layouts necessary for covering the long-tail distributions of real-world scenes.
blocks.zh: 为规避这个内存瓶颈,以代理为主的基因学方法[45,35](图1 (b))已经作为一种高效的替代品出现,它通过数据倒置或全球统计匹配绕过双层优化. 由于全球统计匹配无法全面描述多类的复杂空间安排,现有方法,如物体检测方法[27]或通用数据集分馏方法[26],转而依靠真实数据的固定空间口罩进行结构规范化. 这一策略将模型简化为静态边界内单纯的纹理填充器,而不是真正的场景作曲家,因此无法合成一套紧凑而翔实的空间布局来覆盖真实世界场景的长尾分布.

blocks.en: To bridge these gaps, we propose a novel S ample- S et R einforcement L earning (S 2 -RL) framework for generative semantic segmentation dataset distillation (SSDD), as shown in Figure 1(c) . Unlike existing gradient-heavy or mask-conditioned methods, we reformulate SSDD as a diffusion-based text-to-image generation paradigm and optimize it through reward-driven reinforcement learning without pixel-wise gradient unrolling through downstream segmentation training. By framing the generative model as an agent, S 2 -RL directly utilizes appropriate rewards to drive policy updates. This framework not only eliminates the need for heavy second-order gradient computations, but also empowers the model to flexibly synthesize a compact set of images with novel, informative contents from concise text prompts, thus enabling effective SSDD.
blocks.zh: 为了弥补这些差距,我们提议用图1(c)所示的小说S Full-S et R einforcement L(S 2-RL)框架来进行基因语义分解数据集蒸馏。 与现有的梯度重或有口罩条件的方法不同,我们重塑了SSDD,作为以传播为基础的文本到图像生成范式,并通过奖励驱动的强化学习来优化它,而不通过下游分解训练进行像素相向梯度解滚动. S2-RL通过将基因模型设定为一种物剂,直接利用适当的奖励来推动政策更新。 这一框架不仅消除了重二等梯度计算的必要性,而且使模型能够灵活地从简洁的文字提示中合成一套带有新颖,内容丰富的紧凑图像,从而使SSDD成为有效的.

blocks.en: However, applying RL to generative dataset distillation introduces a new challenge. Standard RL methods (e.g., DDPO [ 2 ] , Flow-GRPO [ 21 , 38 ] ) are typically designed for sample-level optimization, aiming to maximize the quality of individual instances. In contrast, dataset distillation is fundamentally a set-level optimization problem: the objective is to construct a collective dataset that covers the original dataset distribution with fewer samples. Straightforwardly applying standard RL is prone to incur model collapse, where the model over-optimizes for easy patterns while ignoring the long-tail distribution characteristics of real datasets. To address this problem, we introduce a sample-set dual reward mechanism. At the sample-level, for each individual generated sample, we enforce semantic alignment with the input prompt while penalizing collapsed local textures within the same class. At the set-level, we maximize inter-sample semantic distribution diversity by solving a contextual multi-armed bandit problem, enabling the generated compact sample set to appropriately cover the original long-tail dataset distribution. Empirical evaluations on ADE20K [ 51 ] and COCO [ 20 ] benchmarks demonstrate that S 2 -RL outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, reconciling generation quality with distributional diversity.
blocks.zh: 然而,将RL应用于基因数据集分馏带来了新的挑战. 标准RL方法(例如:DDPO [2],Flow-GRPO [21,38])一般是为样本一级优化而设计的,目的是最大限度地提高单个实例的质量. 相形之下,数据集蒸馏从根本上来说是一个设置级优化问题:目标是构建一个以较少样本覆盖原始数据集分布的集体数据集. 直通地应用标准RL容易发生模型倒塌,其中模型过度优化了简单模式而忽略了真实数据集的长尾分布特征. 为了解决这个问题,我们采用了一个抽样的双重奖励机制。 在样本一级,对于每个生成的样本,我们执行语义上与输入速率的对接,同时惩罚同一类中倒塌的局部纹理. 在设定层面,我们通过解决上下文多臂强盗问题,使所生成的紧凑样板能够适当覆盖原长尾数据集分布,来最大限度地实现相模语义分布多样性. 对ADE20K[51]和COCO[20]基准的实证评价表明,S 2-RL优于最新基准,使生成质量与分布多样性相协调。

blocks.en: Our main contributions are summarized as follows: • We propose S 2 -RL, a novel generative dataset distillation framework that leverages RL to enable efficient image synthesis for dense prediction tasks, bypassing the memory bottlenecks of explicit gradient matching. • We design a dual reward mechanism that balances sample quality and set diversity, mitigating semantic mode collapse. • We obtain new state-of-the-art SSDD performance on ADE20K and COCO datasets.
blocks.zh: 我们的主要贡献概述如下: 我们提出S 2-RL,是一种新的基因数据集分馏框架,利用RL来为密集的预测任务提供高效的图像合成,绕过明确梯度匹配的内存瓶颈. ^ 我们设计出一种双重奖励机制,平衡样本质量和设定多样性,减轻语义模式崩溃. ^ 我们在ADE20K和COCO数据集上获得了最新的SSDD性能.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: 2.1 Data-Efficient Learning
blocks.zh: 2.1 数据有效学习

blocks.en: Coreset Selection. This paradigm selects a representative subset from the original data. Classical methods include random selection, which samples data stochastically, and uniform selection, which ensures balanced sampling across categories. Beyond these, geometry-based methods leverage feature space structures. Herding [ 41 , 6 ] selects samples closest to the cluster center of each class to approximate the mean of the distribution. Conversely, K-Center [ 11 , 30 ] aims to minimize the maximum distance between any data point and the selected subset, effectively prioritizing boundary samples to maximize geometric coverage. While efficient, these extraction-based methods are inherently bounded by the finite samples available in the source domain, limiting their ability to bridge distributional gaps through synthesis.
blocks.zh: Coreset选择. 此范式从原始数据中选择一个代表性子集. 古典方法包括随机选择,随机抽取数据进行抽取,并统一选择,确保各类抽样的平衡. 除此之外,以几何学为基础的方法利用空间结构。 放牧 [41, 6] 选取最靠近每类群集中心的样本,以大致表示分布的平均值. 反之,K-Center [11,30]旨在将任何数据点与所选子集之间的最大距离最小化,有效地优先划分边界样本,以尽量扩大几何覆盖. 这些取出法虽然效率高,但本质上以源域现有的有限样品为界,限制了它们通过合成来弥补分布差距的能力.

blocks.en: Optimization-based Dataset Distillation. To synthesize informative data, early methods formulated dataset distillation as a bi-level optimization problem. Gradient matching methods [ 48 , 3 , 50 ] align the gradients or long-term training dynamics of student and teacher models, while distribution matching methods [ 39 , 49 , 28 ] optimize distribution or feature statistics. Differentiable augmentation [ 47 ] , neural feature regression [ 52 ] , and difficulty-aligned trajectory matching [ 14 ] further advance classification distillation. Extending such methods to high-resolution dense prediction remains challenging. In particular, approaches that differentiate through student training face prohibitive memory costs when unrolling pixel-wise computation graphs.
blocks.zh: 基于优化的数据集分解. 为了综合信息性数据,早期的方法将数据集分馏作为双层优化问题. 渐入比对方法 [48, 3, 50] 使学生和教师模型的梯度或长期培训动态一致,而分布比对方法 [39, 49, 28] 优化分布或特征统计. 可分化增生 [47],神经特征回归 [52],和与 [14] 进一步分解分解分解相匹配的难度相匹配的轨道. 将这种方法推广到高分辨率密集预测仍然具有挑战性。 尤其是,通过学生培训加以区分的方法,在不滚动像素计算图表时,会面临令人望而却步的内存成本.

blocks.en: Proxy-based Generative Dataset Distillation. To bypass the heavy optimization, recent works have shifted towards proxy-based generative methods. Model inversion methods [ 45 , 9 , 32 ] invert pretrained model statistics (e.g., BatchNorm) to recover training images. Generative attempts [ 35 , 4 , 53 ] leverage the rich priors of generative models to synthesize diverse data distributions by matching global statistics or embedding alignments. Minimax Diffusion [ 13 ] additionally balances representativeness and diversity during generative training. However, a critical gap remains when transferring these successes to semantic segmentation. Due to the lack of spatial location information in global statistics, existing methods, such as those for object detection [ 27 ] or universal distillation [ 26 ] , typically require pre-defined layouts from real data to constrain the generation process. This dependency limits the synthesized dataset to the topological variations already in the training set, hindering the exploration of novel scene layouts.
blocks.zh: 基于代理的 Generative Dataset Distillation. 互联网档案馆的存檔,存档日期2013-12-22. 为了绕过沉重的优化,近期的作品已经转向了以代理为基础的基因方法. 模型倒置方法[45,9,32]倒置预受训练的模型统计(如BatchNorm)来恢复训练图像. 基因学尝试 [35, 4, 53] 利用基因学模型的丰富的前科,通过匹配全球统计或嵌入对齐来合成不同的数据分布. 最小分泌[13] 在基因训练中额外平衡代表性和多样性. 然而,在将这些成功转化为语义分解时,仍然存在一个重大差距。 由于全球统计中缺乏空间位置信息,现有方法,如物体检测[27]或通用衍射[26],通常需要从真实数据中预设出布局来限制生成过程. 这种依赖性将被合成的数据集限制在已经存在于训练集中的地貌变化上,阻碍了对新场景布局的探索.

blocks.en: Unlike optimization methods that face computational barriers, or proxy methods that depend on static mask priors, S 2 -RL adopts a reward-driven policy optimization paradigm. This allows for the autonomous construction of complex scene topologies without unrolling downstream student-training gradients or using fixed masks as generation conditions.
blocks.zh: 与面临计算障碍的优化方法,或依赖于静态口罩前缀的代理方法不同,S 2-RL采用了奖励驱动的政策优化范式. 这样可以自主地建造复杂的地貌地貌,而不会使下游的学生培训梯度脱落或使用固定口罩作为生成条件.

blocks.en: 2.2 Reinforcement Learning for Diffusion Models
blocks.zh: 2.2 传播模式强化学习

blocks.en: Reinforcement Learning has recently been integrated with diffusion models to align generation with specific objectives. DDPO [ 2 ] treats the multi-step denoising process as a policy, enabling the optimization of non-differentiable reward functions via policy gradient. DPO-Diffusion [ 37 ] simplifies this by leveraging preference pairs to optimize the policy without an explicit reward model. To further enhance training stability, Flow-GRPO [ 21 , 38 ] estimates gradients using the relative advantage of sampled groups, eliminating the need for a separate value network.
blocks.zh: 最近将加强学习与传播模式结合起来,使生成与具体目标相一致。 DDPO [2] 将多步骤去名过程视为一项政策,能够通过政策梯度优化无差别的奖励功能. DPO-Diffusion [37] 简化了这一点,利用优惠对子在没有明确奖励模式的情况下优化政策. 为了进一步加强培训稳定性,Flow-GRPO[21,38]利用被抽样组的相对优势估算梯度,从而不再需要单独的价值网络。

blocks.en: While these methods have successfully improved sample quality, they primarily focus on sample-level optimization. In the context of dataset distillation, our S 2 -RL extends these frameworks to a set-level perspective, utilizing RL not just for individual image quality, but to actively explore and cover the diverse semantic distribution required for robust downstream training.
blocks.zh: 虽然这些方法成功地提高了样本质量,但它们主要侧重于样本一级优化。 在数据集蒸馏方面,我们的S 2-RL将这些框架扩展到了设定的视角,不仅为个人图像质量使用RL,而且为积极探索和涵盖强力下游培训所需的多种语义分布.

blocks.en: 4.3 Set-Level Reward
blocks.zh: 4.3 套级奖励

blocks.en: While sample-level rewards improve individual images, they do not account for the semantic modes covered by other generated samples. To address this, we reformulate the set-level diversity optimization as a contextual multi-armed bandit (MAB) problem [ 34 ] , where the diffusion policy acts as the agent, the prompt c c serves as the context, and the arms are defined as the discrete collection of semantic prototypes specifically constructed for each category. Our objective is to encourage balanced arm visitation within each class, guiding the agent to cover diverse semantic modes rather than repeatedly exploiting frequent prototypes. To operationalize this discrete bandit framework within a continuous generative space, we introduce three key components: Semantic Arm Construction to discretize the feature space into class-specific prototypes; Robust State-Action Mapping to identify the pulled arms from generated images; and Entropy-Maximizing Reward Mechanism to incentivize the exploration of scarce prototypes.
blocks.zh: 虽然样本层面的奖励能改善个人图像,但并不说明其他生成的样本所覆盖的语义模式. 为了解决这个问题,我们将设定一级多样性优化重新拟订为背景多武装强盗问题[34],即扩散政策充当代理人,即时c充当上下文,而武器则被定义为专门为每个类别构建的语义原型的离散集合. 我们的目标是鼓励在每门课内进行平衡的臂部访问,引导代理人涵盖不同的语义模式,而不是反复地利用频繁的原型. 为了在连续的基因空间内实施这个离散的强盗框架,我们提出了三个关键组成部分: 语义臂构件将特征空间磁盘化为特定等级的原型; 强力克-状态-行动映射以识别从所生成的图像中被拉出的武器; 以及 Entropy-Maximizing Rewarding机制以激励对稀缺原型的探索.

blocks.en: Semantic Arm Construction. To define a finite set of semantic arms, we perform an offline discretization of the real data manifold. We employ DINOv3 [ 33 ] to pool normalized features within real class regions using ground-truth training masks. For each category k k , K-means with K = 50 K=50 centers partitions the region features, and each center is mapped to its nearest observed same-class region feature. These representatives form the discrete arm set 𝒫 k \mathcal{P}_{k} , serving as the reference for set-level coverage. If fewer than K K regions are available, all are retained. Appendix D.4 compares this construction with random same-class representatives.

blocks.en: Datasets and Metrics. We evaluate our framework on two challenging benchmarks: ADE20K [ 51 ] and COCO [ 20 ] . For COCO, we utilize the panoptic annotations converted into semantic segmentation masks to ensure high-quality pixel-wise supervision. As one of the first systematic studies of dataset distillation specifically tailored to semantic segmentation, we establish a standardized evaluation protocol adapted from the image classification task’s images per class (IPC) metric; specifically, considering the multi-class nature of segmentation images, we determine the data budget based on global compression ratios rather than fixed class counts. Accordingly, we set the ratios to 0.25%, 0.5%, 1.0% for ADE20K and 0.625‰, 1.25‰, 2.5‰ for the larger COCO dataset to align with standard distillation scales (e.g., 10/20/50 IPC). We report mean intersection over union (mIoU) and mean pixel accuracy (mAcc) as the primary metrics. For the main comparisons, we construct 5 dataset groups and train 5 student seeds per group, reporting mean and standard deviation over the 25 downstream runs.
blocks.zh: 数据集与计量. 我们根据两个具有挑战性的基准评估我们的框架:ADE20K[51]和COCO[20]。 对COCO来说,我们利用被转换成语义分解口罩的泛光学说明,以确保高质量的像素视向监督. 作为专门针对语义分解的数据集蒸馏最早的系统研究之一,我们建立了一个标准化的评价协议,根据图像分类任务的图像每类(IPC)的度量标准进行修改;具体地说,考虑到分解图像的多类性质,我们根据全球压缩比率而不是固定类数来确定数据预算. 因此,我们规定ADE20K的比率为0.25%、0.5%、1.0%,而COCO大型数据集的比率为0.625毛、1.25毛和2.5毛,以便与标准蒸馏尺度保持一致(如10/20/50 IPC)。 我们报告的是结合(mIoU)与像素精度(mAcc)之间的相接点, 就主要比较而言,我们构建了5个数据集组,每组培训5个学生种子,报告25个下游跑道的平均值和标准差。

blocks.en: Baselines. We compare S 2 -RL with two categories of baselines: (1) coreset selection methods: We include Random selection, Uniform sampling (class-balanced), K-Center [ 11 , 30 ] , and Herding [ 41 , 6 ] . We employ a pretrained ResNet-50 [ 15 ] to extract deep features for distance computation in K-Center and Herding. (2) generative baselines: Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium (SD3.5) [ 10 ] serves as our vanilla generative baseline, and UniDD ∗ [ 26 ] denotes our reproduced UniDD-inspired proxy-guided segmentation baseline. Implementation details of UniDD ∗ are provided in Appendix B.2 .
blocks.zh: 基线。 我们比较S 2-RL与两类基线:(1) 核心集选择方法: 我们包括随机选择、统一取样(分类平衡)、K中心[11、30]和放牧[41、6]。 我们使用一个经过预先训练的ResNet-50 [15] 来提取在K-Center和Herding进行远程计算时的深层特性. (2) 基因基准:稳定扩散3.5中(SD3.5)[10]作为我们的香草基因基准,UniDD*[26]表示我们复制的UniDD所启发的代用分化基准。 附录B.2提供了UniDD*的执行情况详情。

blocks.en: Implementation Details. (1) RL and Set Construction: We employ Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium [ 10 ] as the policy backbone, fine-tuned via LoRA [ 17 ] with a rank of 32. To construct the text conditioning, we utilize the image subset selected by the Uniform baseline. Specifically, we extract all category names present in each selected image and concatenate them into a comma-separated string (e.g., “person, car, tree”) to serve as the multi-category prompt. The policy is optimized using AdamW [ 24 ] at learning rate 1e-4. After policy adaptation, we generate candidate images and screen them using the same sample-level and set-level reward functions used in training. A pretrained teacher model then supplies pixel-wise pseudo-labels for the retained images. (2) Evaluation Stage: We independently train a student on each synthesized dataset using MMSegmentation [ 8 ] . Our default student is SegFormer-B5 [ 43 ] , whose MiT-B5 backbone is initialized from ImageNet-1K-pretrained weights for each run. The models are trained for 200 epochs using the AdamW optimizer with a crop size of 512 × 512 512\times 512 . Additional architectural variations are detailed in the ablation studies.

blocks.en: Quantitative Analysis. Tables and 1 present the results on ADE20K and COCO, where S 2 -RL consistently achieves the best performance among the compared methods across all compression ratios. Compared with coreset selection strategies, the advantage is particularly evident at low data ratios, where limited image budgets make redundancy more costly. While selection draws from a fixed pool of real images, S 2 -RL shapes the semantic content and coverage of new training examples through reward-guided synthesis. The DINOv3-based coreset comparison in Appendix D.1 provides a complementary evaluation with stronger selection features. S 2 -RL also demonstrates a clear advantage over the generative baseline. This highlights the role of RL-driven alignment: while SD3.5 possesses strong general visual priors, S 2 -RL steers generation toward informative supervision for downstream semantic segmentation. Additional controls appear in Appendix B.6 .

blocks.en: Qualitative Analysis. We visualize the latent feature distributions in Figure . A pretrained ResNet-50 extracts class-wise embeddings for Real Data ( ), the Uniform Selection Baseline ( ), and S 2 -RL ( ). In these projections, Uniform samples concentrate around densely populated regions, whereas S 2 -RL samples occupy broader regions of the class-wise feature space. This pattern is consistent with the set-level reward, which favors underrepresented semantic prototypes alongside sample-level quality. For a compact segmentation dataset, covering a wider range of class-specific appearances can provide more varied supervision within the same image budget.

blocks.en: Semantic and Layout Coverage. To complement the feature-space visualization, Table 3 evaluates spatial occupancy, category co-occurrence, and relative geometry using a frozen OneFormer [ 18 ] outside the reward pipeline. Occupancy describes where each class appears, category pairs capture which classes occur together, and relative geometry describes their spatial relationships. The same annotator is applied to generated images and held-out real references. S 2 -RL broadens occupancy and relative-geometry coverage while increasing category-pair recall. Images containing the same categories can still differ in object placement and relative scale. Covering these configurations exposes the student to varied spatial contexts within a fixed image budget. The category-pair results also reveal a coverage–precision trade-off as the range of generated combinations expands. These complementary measurements connect the distributional view to semantic content and scene organization relevant to dense prediction. Definitions and complete results appear in Appendix E .

blocks.en: Semantic Richness. We assess data quality with the complex-scene examples in Figure 3 . While the SD3.5 baseline generates texturally plausible images, it often omits objects requested in dense prompts, such as specific furniture in Row 4 or distinct vehicles in Row 2. In contrast, S 2 -RL synthesizes scenes with higher semantic density, retaining richer structure and detail, from the foliage in Row 1 to the cluttered interior decor in Row 4. Such multi-category scenes provide supervision for several semantic regions and their shared context within each training image. This is valuable for dense prediction, where the student learns object appearance together with its surrounding scene structure. blocks.en: 6 Conclusion and Future Work
blocks.zh: 6. 结论和今后的工作

blocks.en: We propose S 2 -RL, a generative framework for semantic segmentation dataset distillation that fine-tunes Stable Diffusion via GRPO with a sample-set dual reward, integrating sample-level fidelity and set-level coverage to bypass the computational bottlenecks of bi-level optimization and the static-prior limitation of proxy-based methods. Experiments on ADE20K and COCO show consistent state-of-the-art gains, and our RL-driven paradigm offers a scalable path toward distillation for broader dense-prediction tasks. The framework incurs an upfront policy-adaptation cost and depends on pretrained generative and segmentation priors. Its rewards approximate downstream utility, and pseudo-labels may inherit teacher errors on rare or ambiguous categories. Future work could reduce adaptation and sampling costs, improve pseudo-label reliability through uncertainty-aware annotation, and incorporate lightweight student feedback to better align reward optimization with segmentation performance without full gradient unrolling.
blocks.zh: 我们提出S 2-RL,作为语义分解数据集分馏的基因框架,通过GRPO来微调稳定分化,并带有样本设置的双重奖励,整合样本层次的忠诚度和设定层次的覆盖度来绕过双层次优化的计算瓶颈和基于代理方法的静态先行限制. 关于ADE20K和COCO的实验显示了一致的最新成果,我们的RL驱动范式为更广泛的密集预测任务提供了可扩展的蒸馏路径. 该框架需要先行的政策调整费用,并取决于事先经过培训的基因分化和分化前科。 它的奖励大致相当于下游的效用,而伪标签可能继承罕见或模糊类别的教师错误。 未来的工作可以降低适应和取样成本,通过对不确定性的认知注释来提高伪标签的可靠性,并纳入轻量级学生反馈,以更好地将奖励优化与分解性能相配合而无需完全梯度分解.

blocks.en: Policy Model. We utilize Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium [ 10 ] as our backbone policy π θ \pi_{\theta} . To ensure training efficiency and prevent catastrophic forgetting of the pretrained generative priors, we adopt low-rank adaptation (LoRA) [ 17 ] for fine-tuning. • Base Model: Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium (2.5B parameters). • LoRA Configuration: We inject LoRA layers into the attention mechanisms of the MMDiT. The LoRA rank is set to 32, with an alpha value of 64. • Trainable Parameters: Only the LoRA weights ( ∼ \sim 70 MB) are updated during the RL phase.

blocks.en: Reward Models. Our dual-reward mechanism relies on three types of frozen pretrained models, each playing a distinct role: • Semantic Evaluator Ensemble. For ADE20K we use UPerNet-ConvNeXt-Large [ 42 , 23 ] , SegFormer-B5 [ 43 ] , and DPT-Large [ 29 ] ; for COCO we use Mask2Former-Swin-Large [ 7 ] , EOMT-Large [ 19 ] , and EOMT-Base. Each frozen evaluator computes alignment from its own mask and diversity from its own intermediate feature grid, using at most 100 locations per predicted class. We sum the resulting scalar sample rewards. Raw feature vectors from different architectures are never compared. Per-pixel majority voting combines the masks only for DINOv3 region pooling in the set-level reward. • Pseudo-Label Teacher. The downstream student is trained on synthesized images paired with pseudo-labels produced by a single, stronger frozen segmentor: UPerNet-ConvNeXt-XLarge for ADE20K and Mask2Former-Swin-Large for COCO. The same teacher is used to label images from all synthetic baselines (SD3.5, UniDD ∗ , and S 2 -RL), so the annotation procedure and downstream training protocol are shared across methods. • Feature Extractor. The set-level reward (Eq. 7 ) is computed on dense patch features from a frozen DINOv3 ViT-L model [ 33 ] . The semantic mask from the segmentor ensemble is downsampled by nearest-neighbor interpolation to match the DINOv3 patch grid, and DINOv3 features are L 2 -normalized along the channel dimension before any cosine-similarity computation. DINOv3 is used only for semantic-arm construction and matching in R s ​ e ​ t R_{set} .

blocks.en: B.2 UniDD-inspired Proxy-guided Baseline
blocks.zh: B.2 受UniDD启发的代理制导基准

blocks.en: We implement a UniDD-inspired proxy-guided baseline as an additional generative comparison. UniDD [ 26 ] uses task-specific proxy models to extract task-relevant supervision and guide diffusion-based dataset distillation. Since the official UniDD implementation is not publicly available, we implement a segmentation-oriented proxy-guided baseline using a released pretrained FreestyleNet [ 44 ] checkpoint as the layout-to-image generator, while following the proxy-guided sampling and refinement principle of UniDD. This implementation corresponds to the UniDD ∗ entries in Table and Table 1 .
blocks.zh: 我们实施一个受UniDD启发的代理指导基线,作为额外的基因比较。 UniDD [26] 使用特定任务代用模型来提取与任务相关的监督并指导基于扩散的数据集蒸馏. 由于UniDD的正式实施不公开,我们采用已放行的预先训练的FreestyleNet[44]检查站作为布局到图像生成器,同时遵循UniDD的代理制取和完善原则,实施分化导向的代理制取基准. 这一执行与表1中的UniDD *条目一致。

blocks.en: The proxy-guided baseline initializes generation from the masks selected by the Uniform baseline. This keeps the layout source and compression budget aligned with the real-data subset baselines, while replacing the corresponding real images with generated images. FreestyleNet takes dense semantic layouts as conditions and synthesizes images aligned with the input masks, making it suitable for adapting proxy-guided generation to semantic segmentation.
blocks.zh: 代理制导基准从统一基准选定的口罩中初始化生成. 这保持了布局源和压缩预算与真数据子集基线一致,同时用生成的图像来取代相应的真图像. FreestyleNet将稠密的语义布局作为条件,并合成了与输入口罩一致的图像,使其适合将代用制导生成适应语义分解.

blocks.en: The proxy segmentation model is dataset-specific. For ADE20K, we use SegFormer-B0 as the proxy segmentation model. For COCO, we use MaskFormer-R50 as the proxy segmentation model. During generation, the proxy model scores the semantic consistency between the generated image and the input mask, and this score is used for refinement and filtering. After image generation, we use the same pseudo-labeling teacher as S 2 -RL to obtain pixel-wise annotations, so that all synthetic baselines are evaluated with the same downstream training pipeline.
blocks.zh: 代理分解模型是数据集特异性的. 对于ADE20K,我们使用SegFormer-B0作为代理分区模型. 对于COCO,我们使用MaskFormer-R50作为代理分化模型. 在生成过程中,代理模型对生成的图像和输入口罩之间的语义一致性进行评分,这个分数用于精度和过滤. 在图像生成后,我们使用与S 2-RL相同的伪标签老师来获得像素相向的注释,这样所有合成基线都会用相同的下游训练管进行评价.

blocks.en: We follow the original UniDD hyperparameter setting as closely as possible. Each image is generated with 250 sampling steps. The filtering threshold is set to 0.75. A generated image is accepted if its proxy score exceeds this threshold. If the proxy score remains below the threshold for three consecutive attempts, we keep the highest-scoring image among the attempted samples. This fallback rule preserves a fixed dataset size for every compression ratio and prevents failed generations from changing the number of downstream training images.
blocks.zh: 我们尽可能密切地跟踪UniDD超参数设置。 每个图像都是用250个取样步骤生成的. 过滤阈值被设定为0.75. 如果一个生成的图像的代理得分超过这个阈值,则被接受. 如果代理得分连续三次保持在阈值以下,我们在尝试样本中保持得分最高的图像. 这个倒置规则为每个压缩比保留了固定的数据集大小,并防止了失败的后世改变下游训练图像的数量.

blocks.en: We report this method as UniDD ∗ to indicate that it is a segmentation-oriented adaptation of UniDD rather than the official implementation. Compared with the vanilla SD3.5 baseline, UniDD ∗ uses mask-conditioned generation and task-specific proxy filtering. Compared with S 2 -RL, it does not fine-tune the diffusion policy with sample-set rewards, but instead relies on iterative proxy-guided sampling from the pretrained FreestyleNet generator.
blocks.zh: 我们将此方法报告为UniDD ∗ ,以表明它是针对UniDD的分化调整,而不是正式实施。 相较于香草SD3.5基线,UniDD *使用口罩条件生成和任务特定代理过滤. 相较于S 2-RL,它并没有用样本集奖励来微调扩散政策,而是依赖于从被预训的FreestyleNet生成器中进行迭代代理制取.

blocks.en: We use the zero-KL setting adopted in the GRPO-Guard [ 38 ] training configuration, where the KL loss is not applied. GRPO-Guard stabilizes GRPO-style optimization for diffusion/flow models through regulated clipping, implemented by ratio normalization and gradient reweighting across denoising timesteps. These operations restore more balanced importance-ratio distributions and reduce timestep-wise gradient imbalance during policy optimization.

blocks.en: B.4 GRPO Reward Computation Details
blocks.zh: B.4 GPRO 奖励计算细节

blocks.en: We describe the reward computation process used during GRPO fine-tuning. In each training iteration, we sample 16 text prompts from the prompt pool. For each prompt, the rollout policy generates a group of 8 trajectories for ADE20K or 16 for COCO, each producing one candidate image. Rewards are computed on the final images, while the policy update uses the stored denoising trajectories to evaluate the clipped per-step importance-ratio objective described in Appendix A.1 .
blocks.zh: 我们描述了GRPO微调过程中使用的奖励计算过程. 每次训练时,我们都会抽取16个文字提示 对于每个快件,推出政策为ADE20K或COCO生成一组由8个轨道组成的一组,每组生成一个候选图像. 奖励在最后图像上计算,而政策更新则使用所储存的去诺化轨迹来评价附录A.1所描述的被剪接的每步重要性-比例目标。

blocks.en: For each generated image, we compute the sample-level reward terms, including semantic alignment and intra-class feature diversity. The semantic alignment reward evaluates whether the generated image is consistent with the target semantic content specified by the prompt. The intra-class diversity reward evaluates whether the image contains discriminative class-level features rather than repetitive or collapsed visual patterns. These two terms are computed independently for each image and provide local supervision for sample quality.
blocks.zh: 对于每个生成的图像,我们计算样本级的奖励条款,包括语义对接和类内特征多样性. 语义校正奖励评价生成的图像是否与提示所指定的目标语义内容一致. 阶级内部多样性奖赏评价画面是否包含有歧视性的阶级层次特征,而不是重复或倒塌的视觉模式. 这两个术语是独立计算每个图像的,为样本质量提供当地监督。

blocks.en: The set-level reward is computed on the same generated batch rather than on a separate reward batch. After extracting semantic features from all generated images in the current iteration, each feature is assigned to its nearest semantic prototype. We then accumulate the prototype-count increment induced by the current mini-batch. The set-level reward is evaluated using both the historical prototype counts and the current batch-level increment, before committing the new counts to the global memory. This batch-aware update prevents reward inflation across iterations rather than within a single batch: samples that match the same prototype within a single iteration receive the same exploration bonus, but historical counts are updated only after the entire batch has been evaluated, so later iterations correctly see the marginal coverage contributed by the previous one.
blocks.zh: 设定等级的奖励是根据同一批次产生的,而不是根据单独的奖励批次计算的。 在从当前迭代中所有生成的图像中提取出语义特征后,每个特征被分配到其最近的语义原型. 然后我们累积目前小批量引起的原型计数递增。 采用历史原型计数和目前的分批分级增量来评价定级奖励,然后将新的计数投入全球记忆。 这个分批的更新可以防止整个重复而不是在一个分批之内的奖励性通货膨胀:一个分批之内匹配同一原型的样本会得到同样的勘探奖金,但历史计数只有在整批被评价后才会更新,所以后来的分批正确看到前一分批贡献的边际覆盖.

blocks.en: After combining the sample-level and set-level rewards, GRPO computes advantages within each same-prompt group. Specifically, the G G rewards belonging to one prompt are normalized within that group, and the resulting advantages are clipped to [ − 5 , 5 ] [-5,5] before use in the surrogate. We do not normalize rewards across all 16 prompts in the iteration. This design ensures that the policy compares alternative generations under the same semantic condition, rather than mixing reward scales across unrelated prompts.
blocks.zh: GRPO在合并了样本级和定级奖励后,计算出每个同时组内的优势. 具体地说,属于一个快件的G奖项在该组内实现正常化,由此产生的优势被剪去到[−5,5][5,5]后用于代孕. 我们没有将所有16个催促因素的奖励正常化。 这种设计确保了政策在相同的语义条件下比较替代世代,而不是将奖励尺度混入无关的提示.

blocks.en: The sample-level and set-level rewards serve different roles in optimization. The sample-level rewards guide each individual image toward semantic correctness and feature discriminability. The set-level reward tracks prototype visitation during policy training and assigns larger bonuses to under-covered semantic modes. Therefore, the set-level reward does not duplicate the sample-level objectives; instead, it introduces a dataset-level exploration signal that encourages the policy to construct a more balanced and informative synthetic set.
blocks.zh: 样本级和设定级奖励在优化中起到不同的作用. 样本一级的奖励指导每个个人形象走向语义正确性,并突出歧视性。 设定等级的奖励跟踪政策培训期间的原型参观,并给覆盖不足的语义模式分配了更大的奖金. 因此,设定级别的奖励并不重复样本级别的目标;相反,它引入了数据集级别探索信号,鼓励政策构建一个更加平衡和内容更加丰富的合成集.

blocks.en: D.2 Impact of Reward Balancing Weights

blocks.en: The total reward in Eq. 8 is a weighted sum of alignment ( γ a \gamma_{a} ), diversity ( γ d \gamma_{d} ), and scarcity ( γ s \gamma_{s} ) terms. We investigate the sensitivity of the downstream performance to variations in these weights.
blocks.zh: Eq. 8中的总奖励额是配对(γ a\gamma_{a})、多样性(γ d\gamma_{d})和稀缺(γ s\gamma_{s})的加权总和。 我们调查下游表现对这些重量变化的敏感性。

blocks.en: Analysis. As shown in Table 9 , S 2 -RL demonstrates remarkable robustness to hyperparameter variations. While the optimal configuration ( γ d = 5.0 , γ s = 3.0 \gamma_{d}=5.0,\gamma_{s}=3.0 ) yields a peak mIoU of 15.43%, deviating from these values results in only marginal fluctuations. Notably, even when the diversity weight is drastically increased to 10.0 or the scarcity weight is adjusted, the model consistently maintains a mIoU above 14.66%, with a maximum performance drop of less than 0.8%. This stability indicates that our framework relies on the intrinsic synergy of the proposed reward components rather than precise hyperparameter tuning, ensuring reliable performance across a broad range of settings.
blocks.zh: 分析。 如表9所示,S 2-RL显示出超参数变化的显著强度。 虽然最佳配置(γ d = 5.0,γ s = 3.0\gamma_{d}= 5.0,\gamma_{s}= 3.0)的mIoU的峰值为15.43%,偏离这些值只能导致边际波动. 值得注意的是,即使多样性的重量大幅度地增加到了10.0或稀缺的重量被调整,该模型始终维持在14.66%以上,最大性能下降不到0.8%。 这种稳定性表明,我们的框架依靠拟议奖励部分的内在协同作用,而不是精确的超参数调取,确保各种环境的可靠业绩。

blocks.en: D.3 GRPO Group Size and Policy Variability
blocks.zh: D.3 GRPO 小组的规模和政策可变性

Analysis. As shown in Table 10 , increasing G G stabilizes the gradient estimate, leading to faster convergence and higher final mIoU. However, the performance saturates around G = 8 G=8 , after which the computational overhead outweighs the marginal gains. We choose G = 8 G=8 for ADE20K; the COCO configuration uses G = 16 G=16 .
blocks.zh: 分析。 如表10所显示,G的上升稳定了梯度估计,导致更快的趋同和更高的最终MIOU. 然而,性能饱和度在G=8G=8左右,之后计算间接费用会超过边际收益. 我们为ADE20K选择G=8G=8;COCO配置使用G=16G=16.

blocks.en: Independent policy runs. We independently train three S 2 -RL policies on ADE20K and evaluate their 1.0% constructed sets with SegFormer-B5. After averaging downstream student-seed results within each policy, the mean and standard deviation across policies are 25.18 ± 0.30 25.18\pm 0.30 mIoU and 35.90 ± 0.77 35.90\pm 0.77 mAcc. This measures policy-training variation alongside the variation across constructed sets and student seeds reported in the main comparison.
blocks.zh: 独立政策运行. 我们独立地在ADE20K上培训了三套S 2-RL政策,并用SegFormer-B5来评价它们所构建的1.0%的套装. 在每项政策中平均取得下游学生种子结果之后,政策之间的平均和标准偏差是25.18±0.30 25.18\pm 0.30 mIoU和35.90±0.77 35.90\pm 0.77 mAcc。 这衡量了政策-培训的差别,同时衡量了主要比较中所报告的各类建筑和学生种子之间的差别。

blocks.en: D.4 Prototype Number and Construction
blocks.zh: D.4 原型编号和建造

blocks.en: We study the effect of the number of semantic prototypes, or semantic arms, used in the set-level reward. The main experiments use K = 50 K=50 prototypes for each class. We additionally evaluate K = 25 K=25 and K = 100 K=100 on ADE20K at the 1.0% budget.
blocks.zh: 我们研究设定等级奖励中使用的语义原型或语义臂的数量的影响. 主要实验使用K=50K=50原型,用于每类. 我们还对ADE20K预算进行K=25K=25和K=100K=100的评估。

blocks.en: Table 11 : Effect of the number of semantic prototypes K K on ADE20K at the 1.0% budget.
blocks.zh: 表11: KK语义原型数量对ADE20K在1.0%的预算上的影响.

blocks.en: The results show that S 2 -RL is not highly sensitive to moderate changes in K K . All three settings produce similar downstream performance, with a maximum difference of 0.43 mIoU. The default setting K = 50 K=50 achieves the best result. Increasing K K from 50 to 100 does not further improve performance and leads to larger variance, suggesting that overly fine-grained prototype partitioning may make the set-level reward less stable under a small data budget.
blocks.zh: 结果显示,S2-RL对KK的中度变化不高度敏感. 所有三种设置都产生类似的下游性能,最大相差0.43 mIoU. 默认设置 K = 50 K = 50 实现最佳效果. KK从50个增加到100个并不能进一步改善性能并导致更大的差异,这表明过于精细的原型分出可能会使设定等级的奖励在少量数据预算下变得不那么稳定.

blocks.en: In the current implementation, the same number of prototypes is used for each class. This simple design provides a uniform semantic-arm structure across categories, while the scarcity term in the set-level reward assigns larger bonuses to under-covered semantic modes during generation.
blocks.zh: 在目前的实施中,每类都使用相同的原型. 这种简单的设计提供了跨类别的统一语义-臂结构,而设置级奖励中的稀缺名词则在生成期间为被覆盖的语义模式分配了更大的奖金.

blocks.en: Prototype construction. At K = 50 K=50 , we compare nearest-observed K-means representatives with randomly selected same-class region features. Each representative is an observed region feature rather than a cluster-center vector. Both variants repeat policy adaptation from the same pretrained initialization, keeping the other reward and training settings fixed. Table 12 reports means and standard deviations over five downstream UPerNet–ResNet-50 seeds. The clustered representatives yield better downstream performance, suggesting that prototype placement complements the choice of bank size.
blocks.zh: 原型建筑. 在 K = 50 K = 50 时,我们比较了最近观测到的 K 代表与随机选择的同等级区域特征. 每个代表都是观察到的区域特征,而不是集群中心矢量。 这两种变式都重复了政策调整,从相同的预先训练的初始化出发,使其他奖励和培训环境固定下来。 表12报告指下游5个UPerNet-ResNet-50种子的偏差和标准偏差。 分组代表的下游业绩较好,表明原型安排是对银行规模选择的补充。

blocks.en: D.5 Reward Evaluator Robustness
blocks.zh: D.5 奖励评价员的实力

blocks.en: S 2 -RL uses frozen segmentation models as reward evaluators during diffusion policy optimization. In the main setting, we use an ensemble evaluator to provide a more stable reward signal. We further study how the choice of reward evaluator affects the final distilled set by replacing the ensemble with a single frozen segmentation model.
blocks.zh: 页:1 2-RL在推广政策优化期间使用冷冻分解模型作为奖励评价员. 在主场景中,我们使用综艺评价器提供更稳定的奖励信号. 我们进一步研究奖励评估员的选择如何通过将综艺节目替换为单一的冷冻分片模型来影响最后的分片集.

blocks.en: This analysis keeps the generator prior, RL training protocol, reward formulation, and downstream evaluation protocol fixed. The only changed component is the reward evaluator used during policy optimization. All experiments are conducted on ADE20K at the 1.0% budget using the canonical UPerNet + ResNet-50 downstream student.
blocks.zh: 这种分析使生成器在前,RL培训协议,奖励制定,下游评价协议固定下来. 唯一改变的组成部分是在政策优化期间使用的奖励评价员。 所有实验都使用Canonical UPer在1.0%的预算中进行ADE20K 网通+ResNet-50下游学生.

blocks.en: Table 13 : Reward-evaluator robustness under a fixed SD3.5 generator prior on ADE20K at the 1.0% budget.
blocks.zh: 表13:ADE20K预算1.0%之前在固定SD3.5发电机下的奖励评估员稳健性。

blocks.en: The results show that S 2 -RL remains effective with different frozen evaluators under the same generator prior. Among the single-evaluator variants, SegFormer-B5 achieves the highest mIoU, followed by DPT-Large and UPerNet. The ensemble evaluator performs best, indicating that aggregating complementary segmentation priors provides a more reliable reward signal for policy optimization.
blocks.zh: 结果表明,S 2-RL在以前同一发电机下对不同的冷冻评价员仍然有效。 在单评价器变体中,SegFormer-B5实现了最高的mIoU,其次是DPT-Large和UPerNet. 综艺评价人员的业绩最佳,表明汇总互补的分化前科为政策优化提供了更可靠的奖励信号。

blocks.en: This controlled study separates evaluator choice from the generator prior. Under the fixed SD3.5 prior, the performance improvement of S 2 -RL does not depend on a single reward-evaluator architecture. Instead, the reward-driven generation process remains effective across multiple segmentation evaluators, while the ensemble setting provides the strongest overall result.
blocks.zh: 这项受控研究将评估者的选择与发生器之前的选择分开。 在SD3.5前定型下,S2-RL的性能改进并不依赖于单一的奖励评价架构. 相反,奖励驱动的生成过程在多个分块评价者中依然有效,而综艺设定则提供了最强的整体结果.

blocks.en: Appendix F Limitations and Future Work
blocks.zh: 附录F 限制和未来的工作

blocks.en: While S 2 -RL establishes a new state-of-the-art for semantic segmentation dataset distillation, we identify several limitations inherent to the current framework and outline promising directions for future research.
blocks.zh: 虽然S 2-RL为语义分解数据集分解确定了新的最先进技术,但我们确定了目前框架所固有的若干局限性,并概述了未来研究的有希望的方向。

blocks.en: F.1 Limitations
blocks.zh: F.1 限制

blocks.en: Dataset Construction Cost. S 2 -RL incurs an upfront policy-adaptation cost of approximately 48 GPU-hours, followed by multi-step diffusion sampling. Selection-based methods are substantially cheaper to construct. Although policy optimization avoids differentiating through dense student-training updates, the intended use is offline extreme compression with repeated reuse of a constructed set; the measured generative budget does not establish an end-to-end lifecycle speedup.
blocks.zh: S 2-RL先期政策适应费用约为48 GPU小时,然后是多步骤扩散取样。 选择方法的构建成本低得多。 虽然政策优化避免了通过密集的学生培训更新加以区分,但预期用途是线下极端压缩,重复再利用已建成的一组;所计量的基因预算并没有确立从端到端的生命周期加速。

blocks.en: Dependency on pretrained Priors. Our framework relies on the rich semantic priors encapsulated in the pretrained Stable Diffusion 3.5 and the frozen segmentor reward model. Consequently, the performance of S 2 -RL is bounded by the capabilities of these foundation models. For extremely rare categories not well-represented in the Stable Diffusion training corpus, the policy may struggle to generate high-fidelity textures even with RL fine-tuning.
blocks.zh: 依赖事先受过训练的前科。 我们的框架依赖于预先训练的"稳定分化3.5"和"被冻结分解器奖励"模式所封装的丰富的语义学前科. 因此,S2-RL的性能受这些基础模型能力的限制。 对于在稳定扩散培训中代表性不高的极少数类别,即使经过RL微调,政策也难以产生高纯度纹理。

blocks.en: Pseudo-Label Fidelity. Generated training masks can inherit teacher errors, especially for small or ambiguous regions.
blocks.zh: (原始内容存档于2018-10-12). Pseudo-Label Fildelity. 生成的训练口罩可以继承教师出错,特别是在小或模棱两可的地区.

blocks.en: Reward Proxy Gap. We utilize a frozen segmentor as a proxy to estimate the downstream utility of generated samples. While effective, this is an approximation of the true student learning dynamics. There exists a theoretical gap between maximizing the frozen segmentor’s confidence and minimizing the student’s validation loss. In rare cases, the agent might learn to hack the reward by generating adversarial features that satisfy the frozen segmentor but are less transferable to a student model trained independently on the constructed dataset.
blocks.zh: 奖励代理空隙. 我们用冷冻分解器作为代用 来估计生成样品的下游用途 这虽然有效,但却是真正学生学习动态的近似. 最大程度地使被冻结的部分人信心与最小程度地减少学生的验证损失之间存在着理论上的差距. 在极少数情况下,代理商可能通过生成满足被冻结的分机的对抗性特征来学会黑客奖励,但较少可转让给在所建数据集上接受独立培训的学生模型。

blocks.en: F.2 Future Work
blocks.zh: F.2 今后的工作

blocks.en: Extension to Other Dense Prediction Tasks. The proposed sample-set dual reward paradigm is generic and not limited to semantic segmentation. Future work could extend S 2 -RL to other dense prediction tasks, such as instance segmentation by incorporating box-level alignment rewards and depth estimation by replacing the semantic evaluator with a depth consistency reward.
blocks.zh: 扩展至其他紧急任务 。 拟议的样本设置双重奖励模式是通用的,并不限于语义分化. 今后的工作可以将S2-RL扩展至其他密集的预测任务,例如通过采用箱级对齐奖励和深度估计,用深度一致性奖励取代语义评价员。

blocks.en: Student-in-the-Loop Optimization. To bridge the reward proxy gap mentioned above, future iterations could incorporate feedback directly from the student model being trained. Although calculating gradients through the student involves high memory costs (the original bi-level bottleneck), one could employ meta-learning techniques or periodic reward model updates to approximate the student’s needs without full gradient unrolling.
blocks.zh: 学生入室优化. 为了弥补上述的奖励代理差距,未来的迭代可以直接吸收正在培训的学生模式的反馈。 虽然通过学生计算梯度涉及高昂的内存成本(最初的双级瓶颈),但人们可以使用元学习技术或定期的奖励模型更新来估计学生的需求而无需完全梯度解滚动.

blocks.en: Appendix G Broader Impacts
blocks.zh: 附录G 更广泛的影响

blocks.en: This work studies semantic segmentation dataset distillation under compact data budgets. Its primary positive impact is improving the efficiency of dense prediction research by reducing the number of annotated training samples required for downstream model development. By constructing compact synthetic training sets, S 2 -RL may lower storage, annotation, and iteration costs for semantic segmentation experiments, which can make dense prediction model development more accessible in resource-constrained settings.
blocks.zh: 这项工作研究了紧凑数据预算下的语义分解数据集分馏. 它的主要积极影响是通过减少下游模型开发所需的附加说明的培训样本数量来提高密集预测研究的效率. 通过构建紧凑的合成训练集,S2-RL可能会降低语义分解实验的存储,注释和迭代成本,这可以使密集的预测模型开发在受资源限制的环境下更容易获得.

blocks.en: The method also inherits several limitations and risks from pretrained generative and segmentation models. Since S 2 -RL relies on pretrained text-to-image generators and frozen reward evaluators, the generated samples may reflect biases, artifacts, or category imbalances present in these models or in the original training datasets. If such distilled sets are used without careful validation, downstream models may inherit these biases or perform unevenly across rare or visually ambiguous categories. Therefore, the generated data should be treated as a compact training surrogate for research evaluation rather than as a replacement for carefully curated real annotations in safety-critical applications.
blocks.zh: 该方法还继承了被预先训练的基因分化和分化模型的若干限制和风险. 由于S2-RL依赖于经过预先训练的文本到图像生成器和被冻结的奖励评估器,生成的样本可能反映这些模型或原始培训数据集中存在的偏差、文物或类别不平衡。 如果这种蒸馏机组未经认真验证而使用,下游模型可能会继承这些偏差,或者在罕见或视觉模糊的类别中表现不均匀。 因此,所生成的数据应作为研究评价的紧凑培训替代物,而不是作为安全关键应用中经过认真整理的真正说明的替代物。

blocks.en: NeurIPS Paper Checklist
blocks.zh: 神经病 纸张核对表

blocks.en: 1. Claims Question: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The abstract and introduction state the main contributions of S 2 -RL, including the reformulation of semantic segmentation dataset distillation as reward-driven diffusion policy optimization and the proposed sample-set dual reward design. The claims are supported by experiments on ADE20K and COCO and are scoped to semantic segmentation dataset distillation under compact data budgets. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the abstract and introduction do not include the claims made in the paper. • The abstract and/or introduction should clearly state the claims made, including the contributions made in the paper and important assumptions and limitations. A [No] or [N/A] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers. • The claims made should match theoretical and experimental results, and reflect how much the results can be expected to generalize to other settings. • It is fine to include aspirational goals as motivation as long as it is clear that these goals are not attained by the paper. 2. Limitations Question: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The main text discusses upfront construction cost and possible pseudo-label errors. The appendix further discusses dependence on pretrained models and the reward proxy gap between frozen evaluator scores and downstream student learning dynamics. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper has no limitation while the answer [No] means that the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper. • The authors are encouraged to create a separate “Limitations” section in their paper. • The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be. • The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated. • The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. Or a speech-to-text system might not be used reliably to provide closed captions for online lectures because it fails to handle technical jargon. • The authors should discuss the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms and how they scale with dataset size. • If applicable, the authors should discuss possible limitations of their approach to address problems of privacy and fairness. • While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover limitations that aren’t acknowledged in the paper. The authors should use their best judgment and recognize that individual actions in favor of transparency play an important role in developing norms that preserve the integrity of the community. Reviewers will be specifically instructed to not penalize honesty concerning limitations. 3. Theory assumptions and proofs Question: For each theoretical result, does the paper provide the full set of assumptions and a complete (and correct) proof? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The paper presents theoretical propositions as optimization interpretations. The main text states the high-level proposition, and the appendix provides detailed derivations and supporting propositions for GRPO gradient estimation and the sample-set dual reward mechanism. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include theoretical results. • All the theorems, formulas, and proofs in the paper should be numbered and cross-referenced. • All assumptions should be clearly stated or referenced in the statement of any theorems. • The proofs can either appear in the main paper or the supplemental material, but if they appear in the supplemental material, the authors are encouraged to provide a short proof sketch to provide intuition. • Inversely, any informal proof provided in the core of the paper should be complemented by formal proofs provided in appendix or supplemental material. • Theorems and Lemmas that the proof relies upon should be properly referenced. 4. Experimental result reproducibility Question: Does the paper fully disclose all the information needed to reproduce the main experimental results of the paper to the extent that it affects the main claims and/or conclusions of the paper (regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not)? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The paper specifies datasets, compression ratios, baselines, downstream architectures, evaluation metrics, training schedules, reward definitions, and key hyperparameters. Additional implementation details, UniDD ∗ baseline settings, computational resources, and ablation protocols are provided in the appendix. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • If the paper includes experiments, a [No] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers: Making the paper reproducible is important, regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not. • If the contribution is a dataset and/or model, the authors should describe the steps taken to make their results reproducible or verifiable. • Depending on the contribution, reproducibility can be accomplished in various ways. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed. • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm. (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully. (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset). (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results. 5. Open access to data and code Question: Does the paper provide open access to the data and code, with sufficient instructions to faithfully reproduce the main experimental results, as described in supplemental material? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Code and reproduction instructions are available at https://github.com/00why00/S2RL . Released datasets and policy weights are linked from the repository and hosted at https://huggingface.co/0why0/S2RL . The README covers data preparation, training-set construction, and downstream evaluation. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that paper does not include experiments requiring code. • Please see the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • While we encourage the release of code and data, we understand that this might not be possible, so [No] is an acceptable answer. Papers cannot be rejected simply for not including code, unless this is central to the contribution (e.g., for a new open-source benchmark). • The instructions should contain the exact command and environment needed to run to reproduce the results. See the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • The authors should provide instructions on data access and preparation, including how to access the raw data, preprocessed data, intermediate data, and generated data, etc. • The authors should provide scripts to reproduce all experimental results for the new proposed method and baselines. If only a subset of experiments are reproducible, they should state which ones are omitted from the script and why. • At submission time, to preserve anonymity, the authors should release anonymized versions (if applicable). • Providing as much information as possible in supplemental material (appended to the paper) is recommended, but including URLs to data and code is permitted. 6. Experimental setting/details Question: Does the paper specify all the training and test details (e.g., data splits, hyperparameters, how they were chosen, type of optimizer) necessary to understand the results? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The experimental section describes the datasets, compression ratios, metrics, baselines, downstream training protocol, optimizer, crop size, and training schedule. The appendix further reports RL hyperparameters, reward computation details, downstream training details, and computational resource usage. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The experimental setting should be presented in the core of the paper to a level of detail that is necessary to appreciate the results and make sense of them. • The full details can be provided either with the code, in appendix, or as supplemental material. 7. Experiment statistical significance Question: Does the paper report error bars suitably and correctly defined or other appropriate information about the statistical significance of the experiments? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The main comparisons report mean ± \pm standard deviation over five constructed sets and five student seeds per set. The appendix separately reports three independent policy runs, five-seed prototype ablations, and descriptive variation across five stored sets for semantic/layout diagnostics. The stored-set diagnostics are not treated as independent policy replications or significance tests. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The authors should answer [Yes] if the results are accompanied by error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests, at least for the experiments that support the main claims of the paper. • The factors of variability that the error bars are capturing should be clearly stated (for example, train/test split, initialization, random drawing of some parameter, or overall run with given experimental conditions). • The method for calculating the error bars should be explained (closed form formula, call to a library function, bootstrap, etc.) • The assumptions made should be given (e.g., Normally distributed errors). • It should be clear whether the error bar is the standard deviation or the standard error of the mean. • It is OK to report 1-sigma error bars, but one should state it. The authors should preferably report a 2-sigma error bar than state that they have a 96% CI, if the hypothesis of Normality of errors is not verified. • For asymmetric distributions, the authors should be careful not to show in tables or figures symmetric error bars that would yield results that are out of range (e.g., negative error rates). • If error bars are reported in tables or plots, the authors should explain in the text how they were calculated and reference the corresponding figures or tables in the text. 8. Experiments compute resources Question: For each experiment, does the paper provide sufficient information on the computer resources (type of compute workers, memory, time of execution) needed to reproduce the experiments? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The appendix includes a computational resources table reporting construction cost and peak GPU memory for selection-based baselines, SD3.5, UniDD ∗ , and S 2 -RL. It also states the GPU type used for S 2 -RL fine-tuning and reports the training and inference costs needed to construct the distilled sets. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The paper should indicate the type of compute workers CPU or GPU, internal cluster, or cloud provider, including relevant memory and storage. • The paper should provide the amount of compute required for each of the individual experimental runs as well as estimate the total compute. • The paper should disclose whether the full research project required more compute than the experiments reported in the paper (e.g., preliminary or failed experiments that didn’t make it into the paper). 9. Code of ethics Question: Does the research conducted in the paper conform, in every respect, with the NeurIPS Code of Ethics https://neurips.cc/public/EthicsGuidelines ? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The work uses public datasets and pretrained models for semantic segmentation dataset distillation and does not involve human-subject experiments, private data collection, or harmful data acquisition. The study is conducted as a technical investigation of compact training set construction. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the authors have not reviewed the NeurIPS Code of Ethics. • If the authors answer [No] , they should explain the special circumstances that require a deviation from the Code of Ethics. • The authors should make sure to preserve anonymity (e.g., if there is a special consideration due to laws or regulations in their jurisdiction). 10. Broader impacts Question: Does the paper discuss both potential positive societal impacts and negative societal impacts of the work performed? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The paper discusses potential positive and negative societal impacts in Appendix. The positive impacts include reducing annotation, storage, and iteration costs for dense prediction research, while the negative impacts include possible inherited biases, artifacts, and pseudo-label errors from pretrained generative and segmentation models. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that there is no societal impact of the work performed. • If the authors answer [N/A] or [No] , they should explain why their work has no societal impact or why the paper does not address societal impact. • Examples of negative societal impacts include potential malicious or unintended uses (e.g., disinformation, generating fake profiles, surveillance), fairness considerations (e.g., deployment of technologies that could make decisions that unfairly impact specific groups), privacy considerations, and security considerations. • The conference expects that many papers will be foundational research and not tied to particular applications, let alone deployments. However, if there is a direct path to any negative applications, the authors should point it out. For example, it is legitimate to point out that an improvement in the quality of generative models could be used to generate Deepfakes for disinformation. On the other hand, it is not needed to point out that a generic algorithm for optimizing neural networks could enable people to train models that generate Deepfakes faster. • The authors should consider possible harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended and functioning correctly, harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended but gives incorrect results, and harms following from (intentional or unintentional) misuse of the technology. • If there are negative societal impacts, the authors could also discuss possible mitigation strategies (e.g., gated release of models, providing defenses in addition to attacks, mechanisms for monitoring misuse, mechanisms to monitor how a system learns from feedback over time, improving the efficiency and accessibility of ML). 11. Safeguards Question: Does the paper describe safeguards that have been put in place for responsible release of data or models that have a high risk for misuse (e.g., pre-trained language models, image generators, or scraped datasets)? Answer: [N/A] Justification: The paper does not release a new general-purpose image generator, scraped dataset, or high-risk pretrained model. The experiments rely on existing public datasets and pretrained models, and the generated samples are used for semantic segmentation dataset distillation evaluation. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper poses no such risks. • Released models that have a high risk for misuse or dual-use should be released with necessary safeguards to allow for controlled use of the model, for example by requiring that users adhere to usage guidelines or restrictions to access the model or implementing safety filters. • Datasets that have been scraped from the Internet could pose safety risks. The authors should describe how they avoided releasing unsafe images. • We recognize that providing effective safeguards is challenging, and many papers do not require this, but we encourage authors to take this into account and make a best faith effort. 12. Licenses for existing assets Question: Are the creators or original owners of assets (e.g., code, data, models), used in the paper, properly credited and are the license and terms of use explicitly mentioned and properly respected? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The paper cites the datasets, pretrained models, and software frameworks used in the experiments, including ADE20K, COCO, Stable Diffusion 3.5, FreestyleNet, DINOv3, segmentation models, and MMSegmentation. We follow their intended research-use settings and provide code that relies on users obtaining the corresponding assets from their official sources and respecting their licenses. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not use existing assets. • The authors should cite the original paper that produced the code package or dataset. • The authors should state which version of the asset is used and, if possible, include a URL. • The name of the license (e.g., CC-BY 4.0) should be included for each asset. • For scraped data from a particular source (e.g., website), the copyright and terms of service of that source should be provided. • If assets are released, the license, copyright information, and terms of use in the package should be provided. For popular datasets, paperswithcode.com/datasets has curated licenses for some datasets. Their licensing guide can help determine the license of a dataset. • For existing datasets that are re-packaged, both the original license and the license of the derived asset (if it has changed) should be provided. • If this information is not available online, the authors are encouraged to reach out to the asset’s creators. 13. New assets Question: Are new assets introduced in the paper well documented and is the documentation provided alongside the assets? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The implementation is released at https://github.com/00why00/S2RL , with a README covering dependencies, data preparation, and commands for training-set construction and downstream evaluation. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not release new assets. • Researchers should communicate the details of the dataset/code/model as part of their submissions via structured templates. This includes details about training, license, limitations, etc. • The paper should discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose asset is used. • At submission time, remember to anonymize your assets (if applicable). You can either create an anonymized URL or include an anonymized zip file. 14. Crowdsourcing and research with human subjects Question: For crowdsourcing experiments and research with human subjects, does the paper include the full text of instructions given to participants and screenshots, if applicable, as well as details about compensation (if any)? Answer: [N/A] Justification: The paper does not involve crowdsourcing, user studies, or research with human subjects. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Including this information in the supplemental material is fine, but if the main contribution of the paper involves human subjects, then as much detail as possible should be included in the main paper. • According to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics, workers involved in data collection, curation, or other labor should be paid at least the minimum wage in the country of the data collector. 15. Institutional review board (IRB) approvals or equivalent for research with human subjects Question: Does the paper describe potential risks incurred by study participants, whether such risks were disclosed to the subjects, and whether Institutional Review Board (IRB) approvals (or an equivalent approval/review based on the requirements of your country or institution) were obtained? Answer: [N/A] Justification: The paper does not involve human subjects, crowdsourcing, or collection of personal data, so IRB approval or equivalent human-subjects review is not applicable. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Depending on the country in which research is conducted, IRB approval (or equivalent) may be required for any human subjects research. If you obtained IRB approval, you should clearly state this in the paper. • We recognize that the procedures for this may vary significantly between institutions and locations, and we expect authors to adhere to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics and the guidelines for their institution. • For initial submissions, do not include any information that would break anonymity (if applicable), such as the institution conducting the review. 16. Declaration of LLM usage Question: Does the paper describe the usage of LLMs if it is an important, original, or non-standard component of the core methods in this research? Note that if the LLM is used only for writing, editing, or formatting purposes and does not impact the core methodology, scientific rigor, or originality of the research, declaration is not required. Answer: [N/A] Justification: The core method does not use LLMs as an important, original, or non-standard component. Text prompts are constructed from semantic category names rather than generated or optimized by an LLM. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the core method development in this research does not involve LLMs as any important, original, or non-standard components. • Please refer to our LLM policy in the NeurIPS handbook for what should or should not be described.
blocks.zh: 1. 联合国 索赔问题: 抽象和导言中的主要主张是否准确地反映了该文件的贡献和范围? 答复:[是] 说明: 抽象和介绍陈述了S 2-RL的主要贡献,包括将语义分解数据集分馏作为奖励驱动的推广政策优化和拟议的样本集双奖励设计. 索赔得到关于ADE20K和COCO的实验的证实,范围为紧凑数据预算下的语义分解数据集蒸馏。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指抽象和导言不包括文件中提出的要求。 抽象和/或导言应明确说明所提出的主张,包括文件中的贡献以及重要的假设和限制。 [否]或[否/A]对这个问题的答复不会为审议者所看好。 所提出的索赔应当与理论和实验结果相匹配,并反映在多大程度上可以期望将结果归纳到其他环境中。 只要文件明确没有实现这些目标,就最好将理想目标作为动力列入。 2. 限制问题: 文件是否讨论了作者所做工作的限制? 答复:[是] 说明: 主文讨论前期建设成本和可能存在的伪标签错误. 附录还进一步讨论了对预先训练过的模型的依赖以及被冻结的评价分数与下游学生学习动态之间的奖励代理差距. • 答案[N/A]是指文件没有限制,而答案[否]是指文件有限制,但在文件中没有讨论。 鼓励作者在论文中另设"限制"一栏. 文件应该指出任何强有力的假设,以及这些假设被违反的结果如何有力(例如,独立性假设、无噪声设置、模型精确度、不对称近似只在当地持有)。 作者应思考这些假设在实践中可能如何被违反以及会产生什么影响。 作者应反思所提出主张的范围,例如,如果该办法只在几个数据集或几个运行中测试。 一般来说,经验性结果往往取决于隐含的假设,应当加以阐述。 作者应思考影响该方法执行的因素。 例如,一面相识别算法在图像分辨率低或图像取自于低照明时可能表现不佳. 或语音到文本系统可能无法可靠地用于为在线讲座提供闭门字幕,因为它无法处理技术术语。 作者应讨论拟议算法的计算效率,以及它们如何用数据集大小进行比例。 如果适用,作者应讨论他们处理隐私和公平问题的方法可能存在的局限性。 虽然作者可能担心审查人员会把完全诚实的局限性作为拒绝的理由,但更糟糕的结果可能是审查人员发现文件中没有承认的局限性。 作者应运用最佳判断,并承认有利于透明度的个别行动在制定维护社会完整性的规范方面发挥重要作用。 将特别指示审查人员不要惩罚有关限制的诚实行为。 3. 理论假设和证明 问题: 对于每一项理论结果,论文是否提供了一整套假设和完整的(和正确的)证明? 答复:[是] 说明: 本文提出理论命题作为优化解释. 主文陈述了高层次的命题,附录为GRPO梯度估计和样本设置的双重奖励机制提供了详细的推论和支持命题. 指导方针: 答案[N/A]是指论文不包括理论结果. 二. 支助 纸上所有定理,公式和证明,都应该编号并相互参照. 二. 支助 · 所有假设都应在任何定理的说明中明确说明或提及。 证据可以出现在正文或补充材料中,但如果在补充材料中出现,则鼓励作者提供简短的证明草图来提供直觉. • 反之,文件核心中提供的任何非正式证据应辅以附录或补充材料中提供的正式证据。 • 应适当参考证据所依据的定理和莱玛。 4. 实验结果可复制 问题: 文件是否充分披露复制文件主要实验结果所需的所有信息,以影响文件的主要主张和/或结论(无论是否提供代码和数据)? 答复:[是] 说明: 文件规定了数据集,压缩比,基线,下游架构,评价度量衡,培训时间表,奖励定义,以及关键超参数. 附录中提供了更多的执行细节、UniDD * 基准设置、计算资源、以及废除协议。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果论文包括了实验,审查人员将不会很好地看待对这一问题的回答: 使该文件可以复制很重要,无论是否提供代码和数据。 如果资料是数据集和/或模型,作者应说明为使结果可以复制或核实而采取的步骤。 • 视贡献情况,可采用各种方式实现可复制性。 例如,如果这种贡献是一种新颖的架构,充分描述这种架构可能就足够了,或者如果这种贡献是一种具体的模型和经验性评价,那么就可能有必要使其他人有可能用同样的数据集复制该模型,或者提供对模型的取用. 总论. 释放代码和数据往往是实现这一目的的好办法,但也可以通过详细指示来提供可复制性,说明如何复制结果,访问主机模型(如在大语言模型的情况下),释放模型检查点,或者其他适合进行的研究的手段. 二. 支助 虽然NeurIPS并不要求发布代码,但会议确实要求所有提交文件提供一些合理的可复制途径,这可能取决于贡献的性质. 例如(a) 如果贡献主要是一种新的算法,则论文应当说明如何复制该算法。 (b) 如果贡献主要是新的示范架构,文件应清楚而全面地描述该架构。 (c) 如果贡献是一个新的模型(例如大型语言模型),那么应该有一种方法来访问这个模型来复制结果,或者有一种方法来复制模型(例如,有一个开源数据集或关于如何构建数据集的指示). (d) 我们认识到,在某些情况下,可复制性可能很困难,在这种情况下,欢迎作者说明它们为可复制性规定的具体方式。 就闭源模型而言,可能以某种方式(例如,对已注册的用户)限制对模型的访问,但其他研究者应该有一定途径复制或验证结果. 5. 开放存取数据和代码 如补充材料所描述的那样,该文件是否提供了公开查阅数据和代码的机会,并提供了忠实复制主要实验结果的充分指示? 答复:[是] 说明: 编码和复制说明见https://github.com/00whywhy00/S2RL。 已发布的数据集和政策权重与寄存器链接,主机为https://huggingface.co/0why0/S2RL. README涵盖数据编制、培训组合建设和下游评价。 · 答案[N/A]是指纸张不包括需要密码的实验。 详情请见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy)。 虽然我们鼓励发布代码和数据,但我们理解这也许是不可能的,因此[否]是一个可以接受的答案. 文件不能仅仅因为没有包含代码而被拒绝,除非这是贡献的核心(例如,对于一个新的开源基准). 二. 支助 指示应包含复制结果所需的准确命令和环境。 详情见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy)。 作者应提供关于数据存取和准备的说明,包括如何取用原始数据、预处理后的数据、中间数据和生成的数据等。 作者应提供脚本来复制所有实验结果,用于新的拟议方法和基线。 如果只有一组实验可以复制,它们应该说明哪些实验从剧本中删除,以及为什么。 在提交来文时,为了保持匿名,提交人应公布匿名版本(如果适用)。 • 建议在补充材料中提供尽可能多的资料(附于文件),但允许将URL纳入数据和代码。 6. 实验设置/细节问题: 文件是否具体说明了解结果所需的所有培训和测试细节(例如数据分解、超参数、如何选择、优化者类型等)? 答复:[是] 说明: 实验部分描述了数据集,压缩比,度量衡,基线,下游训练规程,优化器,作物大小,以及训练时间表等. 附录还报告了RL超参数、奖励计算细节、下游培训细节和计算资源使用情况。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 试验环境应在文件的核心中详细介绍,以便评估结果,使之合理。 详细情况可通过守则、附录或补充材料提供。 7. 实验统计意义 问题: 纸质报告的错误是否包含适当和正确定义的信息或关于实验的统计意义的其他适当信息? 答复:[是] 说明: 主比较报告指每组有5个已建集和5个学生种子的±\pm标准差. 附录分别报告了三项独立政策,五种种子原型活化,以及五套储存的语义/放出诊断的描述性变化。 储存的成套诊断不被视为独立的政策复制或意义测试。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果结果附有出错栏、置信间隔或统计意义测试,至少对于支持论文主要主张的实验,作者应回答[是]。 应明确说明错误条所捕获的可变因素(例如,列车/测试分拆、初始化、随机绘制某些参数,或在特定实验条件下的总体运行)。 计算出错栏的方法应加以解释(封闭表单公式、调用库函数、靴子等) • 应给出假设(例如,通常分布式错误)。 应明确出错栏是标准偏差还是平均值的标准出错. ^ 报告1-西格玛出错栏是正常的,但应该说明这一点。 撰文者最好报告2-西格玛出错栏,而不是说如果错误的正常性假设没有得到核实,他们有96%的CI。 二. 支助 对于不对称分布,作者应注意不要在表格或数字对称错误栏中显示会产生超出范围的结果(如负出错率). 二. 支助 如果在表格或图中报告出错栏,作者应在正文中解释其计算方式并参考正文中的相应数字或表格. 8. 实验计算资源 问题:对于每个实验,论文是否提供了复制实验所需的计算机资源(计算工人类型,内存,执行时间)的充分信息? 答复:[是] 说明: 附录中包含一个计算资源表,报告基于选择的基线的构造成本和顶峰GPU内存,SD3.5,UniDD *,和S 2-RL. 它还说明了用于S 2-RL微调的GPU类型,并报告了建造蒸馏装置所需的培训和推断费用。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 纸张应说明计算工人的CPU或GPU、内部集群或云提供商的类型,包括相关的内存和存储。 文件应提供每次试验所需的计算数额并估计总计算数。 文件应披露整个研究项目是否比文件所报道的实验需要更多的计算(例如,初步或失败的实验,这些实验没有把它写入文件)。 9. 道德守则问题:文件中进行的研究是否在各个方面都符合《新IPS道德守则》(https://neurips.cc/public/Ethics Guidelines)? 答复: [是] 理由: 作品使用公共数据集和被预先培训的模型来进行语义分解数据集分馏,不涉及人主体实验,私人数据收集,或有害的数据获取. 这项研究是对紧凑型培训成套建筑的技术调查。 • 答案[N/A]意味着作者没有审查《新IPS道德守则》。 如果作者回答[否],他们应当解释需要偏离道德守则的特殊情况。 提交人应确保匿名(例如,如果由于其管辖范围内的法律或条例而得到特别考虑)。 10. 更广泛的影响问题:本文件是否讨论所开展工作的潜在积极社会影响和负面社会影响? 答复:[是] 说明: 文件在附录中讨论了潜在的积极和消极影响。 积极影响包括减少密集预测研究的注释、储存和迭代成本,而负面影响包括可能继承的偏差、文物和预先训练的基因分解模型产生的伪标签错误。 · 答案[N/A]是指所进行的工作没有社会影响。 如果作者回答[N/A]或[否],他们应解释他们的工作为何没有社会影响,或为何文件不讨论社会影响。 二. 支助 负面社会影响的例子包括潜在的恶意或意外使用(如:造谣、制造假相、监视)、公平考虑(如:采用可能作出对特定群体造成不公平影响的决定的技术)、隐私考虑和安全考虑。 会议期望许多论文将是基础研究,而不是与特定应用挂钩,更不用说部署. 然而,如果有任何否定性申请的直接途径,提交人应当指出。 例如,可以合理地指出,可以利用基因模型质量的提高来产生用于造谣的Deepfakes. 另一方面,不需要指出优化神经网络的通用算法可以使人们能训练出能更快地生成Deepfake的模型. ^ 作者应考虑在技术被作为预期和正确使用时可能产生的伤害,在技术被作为预期使用时可能产生的伤害,但产生不正确的结果,以及因(有意或无意)滥用技术而可能造成的损害。 如果存在负面的社会影响,作者还可以讨论可能的缓解战略(例如,对模型进行严格公布,在攻击之外提供防御,监测滥用的机制,监测系统如何从反馈中学习的机制,提高ML的效率和可获取性)。 11. 保障问题: 文件是否描述了为负责任地发布滥用风险高的数据或模型(如预先培训的语言模型、图像生成器或被刮去的数据集)而采取的保障措施? 答复:[不详]理由: 纸上不放出一款新的通用图像生成器,被刮去的数据集,或高风险的预先训练模型. 实验依赖于现有的公共数据集和预先训练的模型,所生成的样本被用来进行语义分解数据集蒸馏评价. 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件没有构成这种风险。 • 释放有可能被滥用或双重用途的已释放模型时,应采取必要的保障措施,允许控制地使用该模型,例如要求用户遵守使用准则或限制进入模型或实施安全过滤器。 二. 支助 从互联网上取出的数据组可能构成安全风险。 作者应说明他们如何避免释放不安全的图像。 我们认识到,提供有效保障是一项挑战,许多文件并不要求这样做,但我们鼓励作者考虑到这一点并作出最真诚的努力。 12. 现有资产的许可证问题: 纸上是否使用资产(例如代码、数据、模型)的创造者或原始所有者,是否适当记名,是否明确提到并适当遵守许可证和使用条件? 答复:[是] 说明: 论文引用了实验中使用的数据集、预先训练过的模型和软件框架,包括ADE20K、COCO、稳定扩散3.5、FreestyleNet、DINov3、分块模型和MMSEGM。 我们遵循他们打算的研究用途设置,提供依赖于用户从其官方来源获得相应资产并尊重其许可证的代码。 • 答案[N/A]是指该文件不使用现有资产。 作者应引述产生代码包或数据集的原始文件。 作者应说明使用了哪个版本的资产,并在可能的情况下包括一个URL。 许可证的名称(如CC-BY 4.0)应当包括每项资产. 二. 支助 对于某一来源(如网站)的报废数据,应当提供该来源的版权和服务条件。 资产被放行的,应当提供许可证,著作权信息,包件中的使用条件. 对于受欢迎的数据集,使用code.com/dataset的论文拥有一些数据集的许可证。 他们的许可证指南有助于确定一个数据集的许可证。 二. 支助 对于重新包装的现有数据集,应提供原始许可证和衍生资产的许可证(如果已经改变)。 如果这种信息不在网上提供,则鼓励作者接触资产的创造者。 13. 新资产问题:文件中介绍的新资产是否有详细记录,与资产一起提供的文件是否充分? 答复: [是] 理由: 在https://github.com/00whywhy00/S2RL上公布了执行情况,其中的README涵盖依赖性、数据编制、以及用于培训的建设和下游评估的命令。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件没有释放出新的资产。 • 研究人员应通过结构化模板通报数据集/代码/模型的细节,作为其提交材料的一部分。 • 培训、许可证、限制等细节 文件应讨论是否以及如何从资产被使用的人那里取得同意。 二. 支助 在提交时,请记住对您的资产进行匿名(如果适用)。 您可以创建一个匿名的 URL , 或者包含一个匿名的 zip 文件 。 14. 与人类主题有关的众包和研究 关于与人类主体的众包实验和研究,论文是否包括提供给参与者的指示和(如果适用的话)截图的全文,以及(如果有)补偿的细节? blocks.en: Justification: The abstract and introduction state the main contributions of S 2 -RL, including the reformulation of semantic segmentation dataset distillation as reward-driven diffusion policy optimization and the proposed sample-set dual reward design. blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper has no limitation while the answer [No] means that the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper. • The authors are encouraged to create a separate “Limitations” section in their paper. • The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be. • The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated. • The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. Or a speech-to-text system might not be used reliably to provide closed captions for online lectures because it fails to handle technical jargon. • The authors should discuss the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms and how they scale with dataset size. • If applicable, the authors should discuss possible limitations of their approach to address problems of privacy and fairness. • While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover limitations that aren’t acknowledged in the paper. blocks.en: Justification: The paper presents theoretical propositions as optimization interpretations. The main text states the high-level proposition, and the appendix provides detailed derivations and supporting propositions for GRPO gradient estimation and the sample-set dual reward mechanism.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • If the paper includes experiments, a [No] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers: Making the paper reproducible is important, regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not. • If the contribution is a dataset and/or model, the authors should describe the steps taken to make their results reproducible or verifiable. • Depending on the contribution, reproducibility can be accomplished in various ways. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed. • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm. (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully. (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset). (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results.

blocks.en: Justification: The paper discusses potential positive and negative societal impacts in Appendix. The positive impacts include reducing annotation, storage, and iteration costs for dense prediction research, while the negative impacts include possible inherited biases, artifacts, and pseudo-label errors from pretrained generative and segmentation models.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that there is no societal impact of the work performed. • If the authors answer [N/A] or [No] , they should explain why their work has no societal impact or why the paper does not address societal impact. • Examples of negative societal impacts include potential malicious or unintended uses (e.g., disinformation, generating fake profiles, surveillance), fairness considerations (e.g., deployment of technologies that could make decisions that unfairly impact specific groups), privacy considerations, and security considerations. • The conference expects that many papers will be foundational research and not tied to particular applications, let alone deployments. However, if there is a direct path to any negative applications, the authors should point it out.
